title: Purchase And Upgrade £21 Million Office In London
h1: Not directly revealed. Two link titles were returned for the page: "Purchase And Upgrade £21 Million Office In London" [b] and "£21M London Office Purchase & Upgrade" [a]. The first matches the URL slug and is likely the H1/page title; the second may be the SEO/meta title.
summary: Case study of a commercial office acquisition facility. A London-based property developer called Silver Oak Capital after making an offer on a central London office building let to a single tenant, with a purchase price of £21m. The developer's plan was to hold the building until the existing lease expired (about 2.5 years away) while seeking planning permission to add a floor and carry out a high-spec upgrade/refit. Challenge: the developer needed more than 65% LTV at a time when lender appetite for offices was limited, many lenders reducing office exposure since COVID. Silver Oak approached a London-based specialist debt fund keen on value-add office deals. The lender's offer was conditional on the developer directing the remaining rental income to the loan, and the lender was expected to release refurbishment funds once the building became vacant. The borrower was experienced with a record of similar schemes. Outcome: finance secured at 68% LTV, 4.75% fixed rate, three-year interest-only term. The results did not reveal the exact loan amount (whether £21m is the purchase price or the facility is ambiguous in the summaries; one summary says 'arranged £21m' and also 'the purchase price was £21m'), the completion date, or the full 'solution' section, which the search tool said was cut off.
